::: spine
**Everything follows one pattern:** `goal(y ~ x, data = mydata)` — read `~` as **"described by."** In plots the left of `~` is the **vertical** axis, the right is the **horizontal** axis (**x** = e**X**planatory). One variable only? Drop the left side: `~ x`. Chain plot layers with `|>`, never `%>%`.
:::

::: cols
::: blk
### Setup & first look

```
library(mosaic)
library(Lock5Data)
```

```
?favstats
```

*help on any command*

```
dim(df)
names(df)
head(df)
```

*size · variable names · first rows*
:::

::: blk
### One categorical variable

```
tally(~ A, data = df)
```

```
tally(~ A, data = df,
      format = "percent")
```

```
gf_bar(~ A, data = df)
```

```
gf_props(~ A, data = df)
```

```
gf_bar(~ A, data = df) |>
  gf_refine(coord_flip())
```

*sideways — for long labels*
:::

::: blk
### Two categorical variables

```
tally(~ A + B, data = df)
```

```
tally(~ A | B, data = df,
      format = "proportion")
```

*`|` means "for each"*

```
gf_props(~ A, fill = ~ B,
         position = "dodge",
         data = df)
```

```
gf_props(~ A, fill = ~ B,
         position = "fill",
         data = df)
```
:::

::: blk
### One quantitative variable

```
favstats(~ Y, data = df)
```

*everything at once*

```
mean(~ Y, data = df)
sd(~ Y, data = df)
IQR(~ Y, data = df)
```

```
gf_histogram(~ Y, data = df,
             binwidth = 2)
```

```
gf_dotplot(~ Y, data = df,
           dotsize = 0.25)
```

```
gf_boxplot(~ Y, data = df) |>
  gf_refine(coord_flip())
```
:::

::: blk
### Comparing groups

```
favstats(Y ~ A, data = df)
```

```
gf_boxplot(A ~ Y, data = df)
```

***categorical first** = horizontal boxes*

```
gf_histogram(~ Y | A ~ .,
             data = df,
             binwidth = 2)
```

*layout is **rows ~ columns**; the `.` means "nothing here," so panels stack*
:::

::: blk
### Two quantitative variables

```
gf_point(Y ~ X, data = df)
```

```
gf_point(Y ~ X, data = df) |>
  gf_smooth(method = "lm")
```

```
gf_point(Y ~ X, color = ~ A,
         data = df)
```

```
cor(Y ~ X, data = df,
    use = "complete.obs")
```

*`use =` needed when values are missing*
:::

::: blk
### Making a plot presentable

```
gf_point(Y ~ X, data = df) |>
  gf_labs(title = "...",
          x = "... (units)",
          y = "... (units)")
```

```
gf_point(Y ~ X, data = df) |>
  gf_refine(
    annotate("text",
             x = 78, y = 220,
             label = "Palm Beach"))
```

*x, y = where the **text** goes*
:::

::: blk
### Regression

```
mymodel <- lm(Y ~ X, data = df)
mymodel
```

*intercept and slope*

```
predict(mymodel)
resid(mymodel)
```
:::

::: blk
### Collecting data

```
sample(df, 25)
```

*random sample of 25 rows*

```
newlist <- shuffle(myclass)
slice(newlist, 1:15)
slice(newlist, 16:30)
```

*shuffle, then take thirds*

```
set.seed(123)
```

*makes random results repeatable*
:::

::: blk
### Inference

```
t.test(~ Y, data = df)
```

*one mean*

```
t.test(Y ~ A, data = df)
```

*two means*

```
write.csv(df, "mydata.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

*then upload to StatKey*
:::

::: blk
### Working with your data

```
filter(df, A == "Yes")
```

*note the double `==`*

```
mutate(df, new = Y / 7)
```

```
droplevels(df)
```

*after filtering, before `t.test`*
:::

::: blk
### When something breaks

**could not find function** — run `library(mosaic)` first

**object 'Y' not found** — you left out `data =`

**unexpected symbol** — missing comma or parenthesis

**answer is `NA`** — missing values; add `use = "complete.obs"` or `na.rm = TRUE`

**console stuck on `+`** — press **Esc**

**no plot appeared** — you saved it to a name; type the name
:::
